blocks.text: Steroids are lipids whose carbon skeleton is bent to form four fused rings. All steroids have the same ring pattern i.e., three 6-cornored rings and one 5-cornored ring. Cholesterol is a common steroid in animal cell membranes. Animal cells also use it for making other steroids e.g., male and female sex hormones.

blocks.alt: Four fused rings sharing edges: three six-cornered rings and one five-cornered ring, with HO on the first ring, a C=C double bond in the second ring, CH3 groups at two ring junctions and a branched hydrocarbon side chain CH(CH3)-CH2-CH2-CH2-CH(CH3)-CH3 on the five-cornered ring.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 4.37 leaves out cholesterol's OH group on the first ring and the C=C double bond in the second ring, and its caption is printed 'Chdesterol'. Cholesterol has both, as drawn above.

The synthesized anabolic steroids resemble male sex hormone (testosterone) and cause general build-up in muscles and bone mass during puberty in males. In 1950s some pharmaceutical companies produced anabolic steroids for the treatment of general anaemia. Some athletes began using anabolic steroids to build-up their muscles quickly and enhance their performance. Today, anabolic steroids are banned. Anabolic steroids can cause serious physical and mental problems e.g., deep depression, liver damage etc.
